newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt bank AKIB raising capital to 200 mln pounds.
newsitem.headline: Egypt bank AKIB raising capital to 200 mln pounds.

text.p: Egypt's Alexandria Kuwait International Bank (AKIB) said on Sunday it was raising its paid-in capital by 100 million pounds ($29.4 million) to 200 million and invited shareholders to contribute 50 million.
The bank, in which private Egyptian and Kuwaiti investors hold a majority stake, said the capital increase would be by issuing 3,208,707 shares worth 15.5826 pounds each.
Shareholders will pay 15.60 pounds and the offer is open for 30 days from November 18, 1996. All offers to buy the shares must be accompanied by half their value -- 7.80 per share.
A bank official told Reuters the board approved the capital increase last month and would invite shareholders to take part again whenever it needed the next tranche.
Non-Egyptian shareholders must pay for their shares in dollars, the bank said.

AKIB's total capital of 100 million is divided into more than 6.4 million shares, the official said. Some are denominated in U.S. dollars and some in pounds. The shares are rarely traded and the bank last distributed dividends two years ago.

In June, an Egyptian state-owned bank sold 70 percent of its 85 percent stake in AKIB to Egyptian businessmen and employee shareholder associations. Egyptian and Kuwaiti investors hold the remaining 15 percent.
